reason: All sixteen requirements are implemented and tested: 83 tests across six new suites covering FSRS scheduling, adaptive planning, readiness banding, provider-policy routing, MCP capability security with authority isolation, source-grounded retrieval, versioned sourced policy, manual notebook export, and the offline-core guarantee. Two real MCP vulnerabilities were found by the tests and fixed. 29 of 29 meaningful mutations were detected.
real_vulnerabilities_found: MCP path traversal: '/data/drafts/../../../etc/passwd' was ACCEPTED because normalization preserved '..' while still performing prefix containment. Any residual '..' segment is now refused outright.

MCP section forging: untrusted content containing a literal '[INSTRUCTIONS]' produced a second, attacker-controlled instruction block because neutralization handled only code fences. Structural markers are now defanged inside data blocks.
known_limitations: Native provider lanes (Grok/Codex/Claude) are policy-modelled and routing-tested but not live-invoked; no provider logins exist in this environment (PREFLIGHT PF-007..PF-009). This is an external gate, not a completed integration.
Local llama.cpp inference (REQ-014) is registered and classified as an offline capability, but no model process is launched in this node (PREFLIGHT PF-010 remains an external probe).
MCP is an in-process capability and authorization registry; no loopback listener is bound in this node.
FSRS uses published FSRS-4.5 default weights; per-learner parameter optimisation from review history is not implemented and is not claimed.
REQ-012/013 policy data ships as a versioned store with real enforcement, but the store is populated by callers; VECTOR does not ship a curated job-target dataset in this node.
